content: The Meningococcal Group B Vaccine (2-dose series) is approved by the FDA for the prevention of invasive disease caused by Neisseria meningitidis serogroup B. It is indicated for individuals aged 10 through 25 years. The vaccine's approval is based on its ability to elicit an immune response, as measured by serum bactericidal activity against three representative serogroup B strains prevalent in the United States. However, its effectiveness against diverse serogroup B strains has not been confirmed. The vaccine is administered intramuscularly, with two doses of 0.5 mL each given at least one month apart. There is insufficient data on the safety and effectiveness of using this vaccine interchangeably with other meningococcal group B vaccines to complete the vaccination series. Adverse Reactions Common adverse reactions observed in clinical trials include: Pain at the injection site (≥83%) Myalgia (≥48%) Erythema (≥45%) Fatigue (≥35%) Headache (≥33%) Induration at the injection site (≥28%) Nausea (≥18%) Arthralgia (≥13%) Severe myalgia was reported by 3-7% of subjects in some studies, and severe pain was reported by 8% of university students in the UK study. Contraindications The vaccine is contraindicated in individuals with hypersensitivity, including severe allergic reactions, to any component of the vaccine or after a previous dose of the Meningococcal Group B Vaccine. Warnings and Precautions Anaphylaxis: Medical treatment and observation should be readily available in case of an anaphylactic event following vaccination. Syncope: Fainting can occur after administration. Measures should be in place to prevent injury from falls. Latex Sensitivity: The tip caps of the pre-filled syringes contain natural rubber latex, which may cause allergic reactions in latex-sensitive individuals. Limited Protection: The vaccine may not protect all recipients or provide protection against all serogroup B strains. Immunocompromised Individuals: Those with altered immune competence may have reduced immune responses to the vaccine. Pediatric and Geriatric Use Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children younger than 10 years or adults older than 65 years. Pregnancy and Lactation Pregnancy Category B: Animal studies have shown no evidence of harm to the fetus or impaired fertility, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. The vaccine should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed. A pregnancy registry is maintained to monitor fetal outcomes in women exposed to the vaccine during pregnancy. Healthcare providers are encouraged to register such cases by calling 1-877-683-4732. It is unknown whether the vaccine is excreted in human milk. Caution is advised when administering to nursing mothers. Administration Shake the syringe immediately before use to form a homogeneous suspension. Do not use if the vaccine cannot be resuspended or if particulate matter or discoloration is observed. Administer 0.5 mL intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle of the upper arm. Storage Store refrigerated at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. Discard if frozen. Protect from light and do not use after the expiration date. Mechanism of Action The vaccine provides protection against invasive meningococcal disease primarily through complement-mediated, antibody-dependent killing of Neisseria meningitidis. The effectiveness of the vaccine depends on the antigenic similarity between the bacterial and vaccine antigens, as well as the level of antigen expression on the surface of the invading bacteria. Clinical Studies The immunogenicity of the vaccine was evaluated in individuals aged 11 through 24 years. The studies measured serum bactericidal activity using human complement (hSBA) against three representative serogroup B strains. The vaccine's ability to elicit a 4-fold or greater increase in hSBA titers and achieve titers above the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) was assessed. Baseline antibody titers varied across populations. Postmarketing Experience Adverse events reported postmarketing include: General disorders: Blisters at or around the injection site. Immune system disorders: Allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, rash, and eye swelling. Nervous system disorders: Syncope and vasovagal responses to injection. Drug Interactions There is insufficient data to establish the safety and immunogenicity of administering the vaccine concomitantly with other recommended adolescent vaccines. Overdosage Limited information is available regarding overdosage. In case of suspected overdose, contact the National Poison Help hotline at 1-800-222-1222. Brand Name The vaccine is marketed under the brand name BEXSERO®. Patient Counseling Patients, parents, or guardians should be informed about: The importance of completing the immunization series. Reporting any adverse reactions to their healthcare provider. Registering pregnant women who receive the vaccine in the pregnancy registry. Alcohol Interaction The interaction between alcohol and the vaccine has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this vaccine.
